title: Zoe's personal runlog: quick experiment sheet
summary: Compact table for quick on-the-fly inference experiments. Focus: throughput vs prompt template changes; lightweight notes and TODOs.
body:
Purpose:
- Keep a tiny, scannable ledger for ad-hoc runs when debugging latency/cost regressions or testing prompt tweaks.
- Not comprehensive evaluation; personal scratchpad for next steps.

Usage notes / conventions:
- run_id: incremental local id (Z001, Z002...)
- model: short name (rw-large, rw-quant, llama-70b-tilt)
- prompt_template: tag/name, full prompt in notes if important
- temp: float
- max_tokens: int
- batch: requests batched together for this run
- metric: primary metric I recorded (e.g., p95_latency_ms / token_cost / acc@top1)
- cost_est: quick multiply of tokens*unit (very approximate)

Table (CSV for quick copy):
run_id,date,start,end,model,prompt_template,temp,max_tokens,batch,requests,metric,cost_est,notes
Z001,2025-01-09,09:12,09:14,rw-compat-v2,short-instr,0.2,256,1,50,p95=210ms,$0.32,noticed spikes when cache cold; try prefix caching
Z002,2025-01-10,11:05,11:07,rw-quant-8bit,short-instr,0.2,256,4,200,p95=260ms,$0.22,batching improves avg but p95 worse on tail
Z003,2025-01-15,14:00,14:02,rw-compat-v2,long-seq,0.0,1024,1,10,p95=480ms,$0.65,large tokens blow up latency; consider truncation or kv-cache warmup
Z004,2025-01-20,16:20,16:21,llama-70b-tilt,short-instr,0.7,128,2,80,p95=700ms,$1.12,high temp, quality marginally better for open-ended; cost too high for prod
Z005,2025-02-01,10:00,10:03,rw-compat-v2,short-instr,0.2,256,8,400,p95=240ms,$0.18,stable under sustained throughput; note memory bump on node-7

Quick observations / scratch items:
- Warmup strategy: run two 32-token dummy requests on new VM to prime KV cache -> reduces first-request p95 by ~35% (observed Z002 vs Z005).
- Batch sizing: for rw-quant-8bit batches of 4 look sweet for cost but hurt tail latency; for SLA-sensitive endpoints cap batch at 2.
- Prompt template variants: "short-instr" keeps token count predictable; "long-seq" yields high variance. Prefer template tagging to track later.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Automate a tiny script to run 3 warmup requests and measure p50/p95 -> add as preflight for smoke tests. (linked: Linear ISSUE-412)
- [ ] Add a cheap token-estimator to compute cost_est from logs rather than eyeballing.
- [ ] Re-run Z003 with truncation at 512 tokens and compare quality drop (manual eval).

Random notes to self (messy):
- If memory on node-7 spikes again, check process GC & nvlink usage. Slack convo with infra on 2025-01-12: #infra-gpu (link in convo).
- Marcus said try rw-compat-v2 quant profile B (less accuracy hit) — follow up next week.
- Keep this sheet minimal; move consistent experiments to shared_drive when stabilized.

Last quick commands I ran locally (for reference):
# curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"rw-compat-v2","prompt":"<short-instr>","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.2}'
# python scripts/mini_run.py --model rw-quant-8bit --batch 4 --requests 200

End of note.

-- zoe
